title: Democrats Clinch Largest House Majority Since 1992 as Hubbard Defeats Foxx in North Carolina
excerpt: Democrats have won at least 258 seats in the 435-member U.S. House of Representatives — the largest majority held by either party since 1992, according to The A
content:
Democrats have won at least 258 seats in the 435-member U.S. House of Representatives — the largest majority held by either party since 1992, according to The Associated Press.

The 258th seat was clinched Sunday, Nov. 22, when Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th District, after a recount confirmed Hubbard's 330-vote margin out of about 287,000 ballots cast. Foxx conceded following the recount, the AP reported.

Foxx had represented the district since 2005 and chaired the powerful House Rules Committee.

The result is historic by the numbers. Democrats last won 258 seats in 1992, and 257 in 2008. Republican House majorities topped out at 247 seats in 2015-2017, according to Reuters, citing congressional records. Democrats have gained 44 seats so far in this cycle — four more than the 40 they picked up in the 2018 midterms.

Four races remain undecided — in Minnesota and Tennessee, plus two December runoffs in Louisiana — so the final total is not yet settled. Republicans hold at least 173 seats, the AP reported.

The new Congress convenes in January. Democrats will also hold the Senate, setting up divided government with Republican President Donald Trump in the White House.

The incoming majority's reported priorities include addressing high living costs, reversing Republican Medicaid cuts, and restoring Affordable Care Act tax credits that Republicans allowed to expire, the AP reported. Those are reported plans, not enacted law.

What it means for Laredo

For Webb County, the result has a direct local connection: Rep. Henry Cuellar, who represents Texas' 28th District including Laredo, will sit in the majority party when the new Congress convenes in January. Cuellar already backed Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, as Webb Watch 956 reported Nov. 19 — but Jeffries becoming Speaker is not decided; he won the Democratic caucus nomination, and the full House votes in January.

Sources: Reuters, Nov. 22, 2026; The Associated Press, Nov. 22, 2026; Public Radio East, Nov. 23, 2026.
